page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7nex.4xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance within the Enhanced server family, built for enterprise workloads requiring consistent processor capacity and dedicated hardware execution. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz, the instance provisions 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores via hyper-threading. The compute subsystem includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache, complemented by support for AVX-512, DL Boost Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI), and cryptographic acceleration instructions such as VAES and SHA-NI.

Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Benchmark evaluations record large-block uncached memory read bandwidth of 98.36 GB/sec alongside write throughput of 56.31 GB/sec. The instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps managed under KVM virtualization. A key architectural characteristic is the complete absence of bundled local storage, requiring persistent data and operating systems to be attached externally via network block devices.

Performance across synthetic and operational benchmarks reflects solid mid-tier capabilities. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 21,079.2 and a PassMark memory score of 2,609.86, supported by stress-ng results of 1,858.69 on single-core and 15,508.96 on multi-core workloads. In application benchmarks, it sustains 15.47 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a static web serving throughput of 20.58 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression yields 82.89 GB/sec.

Without local NVMe drives or integrated GPUs, this instance trades direct disk I/O latency for standard network-attached storage architectures. Its combination of balanced compute-to-memory density, 20 Gbps baseline network performance, and dedicated Xeon hardware makes it well matched for web serving, microservices hosting, in-memory caching systems, CI/CD runners, and general enterprise databases reliant on managed cloud storage.
